title: Rituals We No Longer Explain
sentences: My family performs a number of small rituals at the end of every single year.
Nobody in it can now explain where the majority of them originally came from.
One of them requires a particular chair to remain empty throughout the whole meal.
As a child I simply assumed that every household did something fairly similar.
When I finally asked my grandmother, she said her own mother had started it.
The reason behind it had apparently not survived even a single generation.
We continue anyway, with something between genuine affection and mild embarrassment.
An outsider watching the whole performance would probably find it faintly absurd.
What the ritual preserves is not its meaning but simply the fact of its repetition.
That may be the only thing a family reliably manages to pass on at all.
